summary: One role cleared every hard gate on October 26: Inato’s Senior AI Engineer, open to the Paris office or fully remote from France. It pays €85,000–€100,000 a year plus equity, and the work is LLM pipelines and agents for clinical-trial recruitment and site selection. It is not a new listing. This site rejected the same requisition on October 14 because its floor was then €70,000; the employer republished it on October 23 with a higher range. Two other leads were already closed: lemlist’s Senior Applied AI Engineer (filled) and a Jus Mundi Staff Engineer listing. These entries are research leads, not recommendations.
coverage: Automated official-ATS sweep on October 26: 131 of 276 attempted Ashby, Lever and Greenhouse board aliases returned data; many failed aliases are likely wrong board names, not evidence of no vacancies. AI-titled roles on reachable boards were screened, as were Paris- or France-located engineering roles with published pay on reachable Ashby boards, Greenhouse and Lever pay data for 120 France-located engineering roles, and Ashby engineering roles first published since October 22 with a France or Europe-remote location. Compared with October 25, no new matching postings appeared. This run also compared every previously reported listing still on a reachable board against its recorded pay and posting date, which surfaced the Inato change. A second pass reached 43 of 300 attempted aliases, and a Workable and Recruitee check reached 6 of 44. Seven web searches were used for discovery only. Six listings were examined individually on employer or job-board pages; one application form rendered. Coverage is bounded, not exhaustive.
criteria: Paris hybrid with explicit attendance, or fully remote explicitly allowing France-based applicants.
Senior/staff hands-on AI-central engineering; an AI employer, coding assistant use or AI product UI alone does not establish the required assignment.

Employer-published annual gross cash-base lower bound strictly above €100,000, or at least €80,000 with explicit equity. Use the lower bound; equity is not cash; packages, OTE, unlabelled pay ranges and estimates do not pass.
No unchanged prior selections. Requisition identity takes precedence over refreshed titles, URLs or timestamps; historical qualification is not current-live verification.
uncertainty: Sources checked October 26, 2026. Posting dates come from employer metadata where published.

Inato’s pay change was visible in this site’s automated sweeps from October 24, but those runs treated the listing as previously reported and did not re-examine it. It is reported today as a material change to an existing requisition, not as a newly discovered role.
Inato’s salary is classified as an annual EUR salary in the employer’s ATS data, separate from equity; the listing does not use the word “gross”. Equity terms (amount, vesting) are not published.
Inato’s current headcount, revenue, profitability and runway are not publicly verified. The latest funding found is a 2023 Series A2; no later round was found.

Previously reported near-misses were rechecked where boards were reachable. Cohere’s agent-security role still publishes pay only for Canada and the US, and n8n’s agent-platform role publishes European regional pay tiers but still does not name France. Their earlier decisions stand, so they were not re-listed.
Deduplication covered the accessible October 10–25 reports and the supplied October 3/5 Escape history.
decision: No approval needed for this authorized daily website update. One role qualified today: Inato’s Senior AI Engineer, after an evidenced pay change to a previously rejected requisition. No applications or outreach were made.

jobs.title: Senior AI Engineer
jobs.locationQuote: “PARIS OFFICE or REMOTE FROM FRANCE”; ATS location type: Remote. The application form adds: “This role requires you to be based in France and already have full authorization to work here.”[1][2]

salary.quote: “€85K – €100K • Offers Equity”. The official ATS data lists €85,000–€100,000 as a one-year EUR Salary component, with equity as a separate component. The listing does not say “gross” explicitly. This site’s archived October 14 report recorded the same requisition at €70K – €95K.[1][3]

reasons: Pay passes the €80,000-plus-equity branch: the published annual salary floor is €85,000 and equity is explicitly offered as a separate component. Equity is not counted as cash, and the €100,000 ceiling does not clear the strict cash-only branch.[1][3]

Material change since this site’s history: the same requisition was rejected on October 14 because its published floor was €70,000. The employer republished it on October 23 with a €85,000–€100,000 range; the location wording and the duty quoted on October 14 are unchanged. The earlier range is in this site’s archived October 14 report.[1][3]

Location passes: the role is open to the Paris office or fully remote from France. The application requires living in France at least six months a year, paying tax there and already holding full French work authorization.[1][2]

AI centrality passes: the engineer orchestrates models over multimodal data, builds RAG over long medical documents and patient histories, and builds agentic systems for patient recruitment and site selection.[1]

Seniority passes on the title. The listing asks for several years with ML or AI at the centre of the work and shipped, maintained LLM features in production; it says AI work limited to prototypes, or a first AI feature shipped in the last year, is probably not a fit.[1]
Language requirement: the application says strong English and French are both assessed, and the engineering team works fully in French. The application form rendered on the check date.[2]
jobs.product: Inato runs a platform that connects pharmaceutical trial sponsors with clinical research sites; its homepage claims 6,000+ sites and 25+ sponsors in 50+ countries (company claims). Its AI products cover site selection and pre-screening that automates chart review against trial eligibility criteria.[6] The listing names two example projects, which are examples rather than guaranteed assignments.[1] The first is a pre-screening tool built on reasoning models and visual RAG, used across hundreds of clinical sites. Inato’s March 2025 arXiv paper describes that pipeline: reasoning LLMs read unprocessed EHR documents as images, with multimodal embeddings for record search. It reports 93% criterion-level accuracy on the n2c2 2018 benchmark and 87% on a real-world set of 485 patients from 30 sites against 36 trials, with chart review taking under 9 minutes per patient on average.[4] The second is a site-selection agent that turns a sponsor’s request into constraints and objectives and calls a mathematical optimizer. An Inato engineer’s November 2025 post describes building it, including flaky tests from non-deterministic LLM calls, checking tool-call sequences instead of only final answers, and inspecting traces with Langfuse.[5] Concrete engineering problems: eligibility reasoning when records are incomplete (the paper attributes the real-world accuracy gap partly to this), evaluation of multi-call agents, and handling patient data, which Inato says is anonymized.[4][5]
jobs.financials: Investment: Inato announced a $20 million Series A2 on March 29–30, 2023, led by returning investor Cathay Innovation with Obvious Ventures, La Maison and Top Harvest Capital; MedCity News reported this brought total funding to $36 million.[8][9] No later funding round was found on the company’s news page or in this run’s searches, so newer financing is not publicly verified. Financial condition: revenue, profitability and runway are not publicly verified; funding does not establish them. Size: a current, attributable employee count is not publicly verified. Recent activity: Inato’s news page lists a September 2, 2026 Fierce AI Innovation Awards win in clinical trial operations.[7] pharmaphorum reported in February 2026 that Brad Cottreau joined as chief commercial officer.[10] The homepage features an October 23, 2026 recap of a SCOPE EU fireside chat with Sanofi.[6]
